title: Inverse-plus-linearized permutations in characteristic three
summary: Determine whether two nonzero linearized polynomials can combine with inversion to form a permutation over a finite field of characteristic three.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and nonzero $\mathbb F_3$-linearized polynomials $L_1,L_2$ over $\mathbb F_{3^n}$ such that $$x\longmapsto L_1(x^{-1})+L_2(x),\qquad 0^{-1}:=0,$$ is a permutation of $\mathbb F_{3^n}$? Construct one such permutation, or prove that none exists for any $n$ and any nonzero pair $(L_1,L_2)$.

scope.domain: Permutation polynomials formed from inversion and linearized polynomials in characteristic three
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find one admissible characteristic-three permutation or prove universal nonexistence over all finite extensions and all nonzero linearized pairs.

progress.summary: After proving nonexistence in odd characteristic at least five, the source isolates characteristic three as the unresolved case.
